segs.e: 1. The Undeclared Points

segs.p: Khemāsutta
segs.e: With Khemā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena khemā bhikkhunī kosalesu cārikaṁ caramānā antarā ca sāvatthiṁ antarā ca sāketaṁ toraṇavatthusmiṁ vāsaṁ upagatā hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time the nun Khemā was wandering in the land of the Kosalans between Sāvatthī and Sāketa when she took up residence in Toraṇavatthu.

segs.p: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sāketā sāvatthiṁ gacchanto, antarā ca sāketaṁ antarā ca sāvatthiṁ toraṇavatthusmiṁ ekarattivāsaṁ upagacchi.
segs.e: Then King Pasenadi was traveling from Sāketa to Sāvatthī, and he too stayed in Toraṇavatthu for a single night.

segs.p: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṁ purisaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then King Pasenadi addressed a man,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, toraṇavatthusmiṁ tathārūpaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā jāna yamahaṁ ajja payirupāseyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Please, my man, check if there’s a suitable (male) ascetic or brahmin in Toraṇavatthu to whom I can pay homage.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, devā”ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā kevalakappaṁ toraṇavatthuṁ āhiṇḍanto nāddasa tathārūpaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā yaṁ rājā pasenadi kosalo payirupāseyya.
segs.e: “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied that man. He searched all over Toraṇavatthu, but he couldn’t see a suitable ascetic or brahmin for the king to pay homage to.

segs.p: Addasā kho so puriso khemaṁ bhikkhuniṁ toraṇavatthusmiṁ vāsaṁ upagataṁ.
segs.e: But he saw that the nun Khemā was staying there,

segs.p: Disvāna yena rājā pasenadi kosalo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṁ pasenadiṁ kosalaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: so he went to the king and said to him,

segs.p: “Natthi kho, deva, toraṇavatthusmiṁ tathārūpo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yaṁ devo payirupāseyya.
segs.e: “Your Majesty, there’s no (male) ascetic or brahmin in Toraṇavatthu for the king to pay homage to.

segs.p: Atthi ca kho, deva, khemā nāma bhikkhunī, tassa bhagavato sāvikā arahato sammāsambuddhassa.
segs.e: But there is the nun Khemā, who’s a disciple of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Tassā kho pana ayyāya evaṁ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato:
segs.e: She has a good reputation as being

segs.p: ‘paṇḍitā, viyattā medhāvinī bahussutā cittakathā kalyāṇapaṭibhānā’ti.
segs.e: astute, competent, intelligent, learned, a brilliant speaker, and eloquent.

segs.p: Taṁ devo payirupāsatū”ti.
segs.e: Your Majesty may pay homage to her.”

segs.p: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena khemā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā khemaṁ bhikkhuniṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo khemaṁ bhikkhuniṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the nun Khemā, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to her:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, ayye, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Ma’am, does a realized one still exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “Great king, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ panayye, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, ayye, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ panayye, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“‘Kiṁ nu kho, ayye, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭhā samānā:
segs.e: “Ma’am, when asked these questions, you say

segs.p: ‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā—
segs.e: that this has not been declared by the Buddha.

segs.p: hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ panayye, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭhā samānā:
‘etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ bhagavatā—
na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, ayye, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭhā samānā:
‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā—
hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ panayye, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭhā samānā:
‘etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ bhagavatā—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
Ko nu kho, ayye, hetu, ko paccayo yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, mahārāja, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
segs.e: “Well then, Great King, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, mahārāja,
segs.e: What do you think, Great King?

segs.p: atthi te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti gaṅgāya vālukaṁ gaṇetuṁ—
segs.e: Do you have any accountant or finger-tallier or reckoner who can count the grains of sand in the Ganges, that is,

segs.p: ettakā vālukā iti vā, ettakāni vālukasatāni iti vā, ettakāni vālukasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni vālukasatasahassāni iti vā”ti?
segs.e: how many grains of sand there are, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of grains of sand?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, ayye”.
segs.e: “No, ma’am.”

segs.p: “Atthi pana te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti mahāsamudde udakaṁ gaṇetuṁ—
segs.e: “Do you have any accountant or finger-tallier or reckoner who can count the water in the ocean, that is,

segs.p: ettakāni udakāḷhakāni iti vā, ettakāni udakāḷhakasatāni iti vā, ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassāni iti vā”ti?
segs.e: how many gallons of water there are, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of gallons of water?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, ayye”.
segs.e: “No, ma’am.

segs.p: “Taṁ kissa hetu”?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: “Mahāyye, samuddo gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho”ti.
segs.e: Because the ocean is deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, mahārāja, yena rūpena tathāgataṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṁ rūpaṁ tathāgatassa pahīnaṁ ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: “In the same way, Great King, any form by which a realized one might be described has been cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Rūpasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho—
segs.e: A realized one is freed from reckoning in terms of form. They’re deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom,

segs.p: seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo.
segs.e: like the ocean.

segs.p: ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.
segs.e: To say that after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists: none of these apply.

segs.p: Yāya vedanāya tathāgataṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, sā vedanā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: Any feeling …

segs.p: Vedanāsaṅkhāyavimutto, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho—
seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo.

‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.
Yāya saññāya tathāgataṁ …pe…
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: yehi saṅkhārehi tathāgataṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, te saṅkhārā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: Saṅkhārasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho—
seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo.

‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.
Yena viññāṇena tathāgataṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṁ viññāṇaṁ tathāgatassa pahīnaṁ ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness by which a realized one might be described has been cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Viññāṇasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho—
segs.e: A realized one is freed from reckoning in terms of consciousness. They’re deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom,

segs.p: seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo.
segs.e: like the ocean.

segs.p: ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upetī”ti.
segs.e: To say that after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists: none of these apply.”

segs.p: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo khemāya bhikkhuniyā bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā khemaṁ bhikkhuniṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then King Pasenadi approved and agreed with what the nun Khemā said. Then he rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled her, keeping her on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aparena samayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then on a later occasion King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. He asked the Buddha exactly the same questions he had asked the nun Khemā, and received the same answers.

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, bhante, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
“Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, mayā:
‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bhante, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
“Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ mayā:
‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, bhante, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
“Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, mayā:
‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bhante, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
“Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ mayā:
‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“‘Kiṁ nu kho, bhante, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, mayā—hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi …pe….
“‘Kiṁ pana, bhante, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṁ mayā—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
“Tena hi, mahārāja, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, mahārāja, atthi te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti gaṅgāya vālukaṁ gaṇetuṁ—
ettakā vālukā iti vā …pe… ettakāni vālukasatasahassāni iti vā”ti?
“No hetaṁ, bhante”.
“Atthi pana te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti mahāsamudde udakaṁ gaṇetuṁ—
ettakāni udakāḷhakāni iti vā …pe… ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassāni iti vā”ti?
“No hetaṁ, bhante”.
“Taṁ kissa hetu”?
“Mahā, bhante, samuddo gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho.
Evameva kho, mahārāja, yena rūpena tathāgataṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, taṁ rūpaṁ tathāgatassa pahīnaṁ ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
Rūpasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho—
seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo.
‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti …pe…
‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.
Yāya vedanāya …pe…
yāya saññāya …pe… yehi saṅkhārehi …pe….
Yena viññāṇena tathāgataṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, taṁ viññāṇaṁ tathāgatassa pahīnaṁ ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
Viññāṇasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho—
seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo.

‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na upetī”ti.
“Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: He said, “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma satthu ceva sāvikāya ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṁ saṁsandissati, samessati, na virodhayissati yadidaṁ aggapadasmiṁ.
segs.e: How the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple fit together and agree without contradiction when it comes to the chief matter!

segs.p: Ekamidāhaṁ, bhante, samayaṁ khemaṁ bhikkhuniṁ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ apucchiṁ.
segs.e: This one time I went to the nun Khemā and asked her about this matter.

segs.p: Sāpi me ayyā etehi padehi etehi byañjanehi etamatthaṁ byākāsi, seyyathāpi bhagavā.
segs.e: And she explained it to me with these words and phrases, just like the Buddha.

segs.p: Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma satthu ceva sāvikāya ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṁ saṁsandissati, samessati, na virodhayissati yadidaṁ aggapadasmiṁ.
segs.e: How the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple fit together and agree without contradiction when it comes to the chief matter!

segs.p: Handa dāni mayaṁ, bhante, gacchāma.
segs.e: Well, now, sir, I must go.

segs.p: Bahukiccā mayaṁ bahukaraṇīyā”ti.
segs.e: I have many duties, and much to do.”

segs.p: “Yassadāni tvaṁ, mahārāja, kālaṁ maññasī”ti.
segs.e: “Please, Great King, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmīti.
segs.e: Then King Pasenadi approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. Then he rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled him, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Anurādhasutta
segs.e: With Anurādha

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā anurādho bhagavato avidūre araññakuṭikāyaṁ viharati.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Anurādha was staying not far from the Buddha in a wilderness hut.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā aññatitthiyā paribbājakā yenāyasmā anurādho tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā anurādhena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then several wanderers of other religions went up to Venerable Anurādha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā āyasmantaṁ anurādhaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and said to him:

segs.p: “yo so, āvuso anurādha, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṁ tathāgato imesu catūsu ṭhānesu paññāpayamāno paññāpeti:
segs.e: “Reverend Anurādha, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them in these four ways:

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā”ti?
segs.e: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.”

segs.p: “Yo so, āvuso, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṁ tathāgato aññatra imehi catūhi ṭhānehi paññāpayamāno paññāpeti:
segs.e: “Reverends, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them other than these four ways:

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā”ti.
segs.e: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā āyasmantaṁ anurādhaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When he said this, the wanderers said to him,

segs.p: “so cāyaṁ bhikkhu navo bhavissati acirapabbajito, thero vā pana bālo abyatto”ti.
segs.e: “This mendicant must be junior, recently gone forth, or else a foolish, incompetent senior mendicant.”

segs.p: Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā āyasmantaṁ anurādhaṁ navavādena ca bālavādena ca apasādetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: Then, after rebuking Venerable Anurādha by calling him “junior” and “foolish”, the wanderers rose from their seats and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato anurādhassa acirapakkantesu aññatitthiyesu paribbājakesu etadahosi:
segs.e: Soon after they had left, Anurādha thought,

segs.p: “sace kho maṁ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā uttariṁ puccheyyuṁ,
segs.e: “If those wanderers were to inquire further,

segs.p: kathaṁ byākaramāno nu khvāhaṁ tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ vuttavādī ceva bhagavato assaṁ, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyaṁ, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākareyyaṁ, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgaccheyyā”ti?
segs.e: how should I answer them so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should I explain in line with his teaching, so that there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anurādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā anurādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Anurādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre araññakuṭikāyaṁ viharāmi.
Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā aññatitthiyā paribbājakā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā mayā saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
‘yo so, āvuso anurādha, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṁ tathāgato imesu catūsu ṭhānesu paññāpayamāno paññāpeti:
“hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti vā …pe…
“neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti vā’ti?
Evaṁ vuttāhaṁ, bhante, te aññatitthiye paribbājake etadavocaṁ:
‘yo so, āvuso, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṁ tathāgato aññatra imehi catūhi ṭhānehi paññāpayamāno paññāpeti:
“hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti vā …pe…
“neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti vā’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
‘so cāyaṁ bhikkhu navo bhavissati acirapabbajito thero vā pana bālo abyatto’ti.
Atha kho maṁ, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā navavādena ca bālavādena ca apasādetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁsu.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, acirapakkantesu tesu aññatitthiyesu paribbājakesu etadahosi:

‘sace kho maṁ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā uttariṁ puccheyyuṁ, kathaṁ byākaramāno nu khvāhaṁ tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ vuttavādī ceva bhagavato assaṁ, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyaṁ, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākareyyaṁ, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgaccheyyā’”ti?
“Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, anurādha,
segs.e: “What do you think, Anurādha?

segs.p: rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: Is form permanent or impermanent?”

segs.p: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

segs.p: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Suffering, sir.”

segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

segs.p: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?
segs.e: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

segs.p: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

segs.e: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Tasmātiha, anurādha, yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: “So, Anurādha, you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, anurādha, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, anurādha,
segs.e: What do you think, Anurādha?

segs.e: “Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to feeling?” …

“Saññaṁ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: “… perception?” …

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
“Saṅkhāre tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: “… choices?” …

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
“Viññāṇaṁ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: “… consciousness?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.e: “What do you think, Anurādha?

segs.p: rūpasmiṁ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies in relation to form?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Aññatra rūpā tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: “Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies apart from form?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Vedanāya …pe…
segs.e: “Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies in relation to feeling?”

segs.e: “… apart from feeling?” …

segs.e: “… in relation to perception?” …

“Aññatra viññāṇā tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.

segs.p: rūpaṁ, vedanaṁ, saññaṁ, saṅkhāre, viññāṇaṁ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to one who has form?” … “… feeling?” … “… perception?” … “… choices?” … “… consciousness?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, anurādha,
segs.e: “What do you think, Anurādha?

segs.p: ayaṁ so arūpī avedano asaññī asaṅkhāro aviññāṇo tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to that one who is without form?” … “… feeling?” … “… perception?” … “… choices?” … “… consciousness?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ettha ca te, anurādha, diṭṭheva dhamme saccato thetato tathāgate anupalabbhiyamāne kallaṁ nu te taṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ—
segs.e: “In that case, Anurādha, since a realized one is not found by you as a genuine fact in this very life, is it cogent for you to declare:

segs.p: yo so, āvuso, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṁ tathāgato aññatra imehi catūhi ṭhānehi paññāpayamāno paññāpeti:
segs.e: ‘Reverends, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them other than these four ways:

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā …pe…
segs.e: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists’?”

“No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu sādhu, anurādha.
segs.e: “Good, good, Anurādha!

segs.p: Pubbe cāhaṁ, anurādha, etarahi ca dukkhañceva paññāpemi dukkhassa ca nirodhan”ti.
segs.e: In the past, as today, what I describe is suffering and the cessation of suffering.”

segs.p: Paṭhamasāriputtakoṭṭhikasutta
segs.e: With Sāriputta and Koṭṭhita (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita came out of retreat, went to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, does a realized one still exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “Reverend, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ panāvuso, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death? …

segs.p: “Etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: Does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death? …

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā:
‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: Does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno, ‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā—
segs.e: “Reverend, when asked these questions, you say that they have not been declared by the Buddha.

segs.p: hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi …pe…
‘kiṁ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
Ko nu kho, āvuso, hetu, ko paccayo yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why they have not been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti kho, āvuso, rūpagatametaṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend, ‘Does a realized one still exist after death?’ is included in form.

segs.p: Na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti, rūpagatametaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Does a realized one no longer exist after death?’ is included in form.

segs.e: ‘Does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death?’ is included in form.

segs.e: ‘Does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?’ is included in form.

segs.e: ‘Does a realized one still exist after death?’ is included in feeling …

Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti, vedanāgatametaṁ.
Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti, vedanāgatametaṁ.

segs.p: Catutthasāriputtakoṭṭhikasutta
segs.e: With Sāriputta and Koṭṭhita (4th)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākoṭṭhikena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita, and they greeted each other.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Mahākoṭṭhita:

segs.p: “‘kiṁ nu kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti …pe…
segs.e: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, does a realized one still exist after death?” …

segs.p: ‘kiṁ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: “Reverend, when asked these questions, you say that this has not been declared by the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
Ko nu kho, āvuso, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Rūpārāmassa kho, āvuso, rūparatassa rūpasammuditassa rūpanirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
segs.e: “Reverend, if you like, love, and enjoy form, and don’t truly see the cessation of form, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ or

segs.p: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
segs.e: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ or

segs.p: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
segs.e: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ or

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Vedanārāmassa kho, āvuso, vedanāratassa vedanāsammuditassa, vedanānirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you like, love, and enjoy feeling …

segs.p: saññārāmassa kho, āvuso …pe…
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: saṅkhārārāmassa kho āvuso …pe…
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: viññāṇārāmassa kho, āvuso, viññāṇaratassa viññāṇasammuditassa viññāṇanirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti …pe…
segs.e: consciousness, and don’t truly see the cessation of consciousness, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Na rūpārāmassa kho, āvuso, na rūparatassa na rūpasammuditassa, rūpanirodhaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy form …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti.
Na vedanārāmassa kho, āvuso …pe…
segs.e: feeling …

segs.p: na saññārāmassa kho, āvuso …pe…
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: na saṅkhārārāmassa kho, āvuso …pe…
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: na viññāṇārāmassa kho, āvuso, na viññāṇaratassa na viññāṇasammuditassa, viññāṇanirodhaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti …pe…
segs.e: consciousness, and you truly see the cessation of consciousness, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Siyā, āvuso.
segs.e: “There could, reverend.

segs.p: Bhavārāmassa kho, āvuso, bhavaratassa bhavasammuditassa, bhavanirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you like, love, and enjoy existence, and don’t truly see the cessation of continued existence, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Na bhavārāmassa kho, āvuso, na bhavaratassa na bhavasammuditassa, bhavanirodhaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy existence, and you truly see the cessation of continued existence, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Ayampi kho, āvuso, pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: This too is a way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Siyā, āvuso.
segs.e: “There could, reverend.

segs.p: Upādānārāmassa kho, āvuso, upādānaratassa upādānasammuditassa, upādānanirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you like, love, and enjoy grasping, and don’t truly see the cessation of grasping, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Na upādānārāmassa kho, āvuso, na upādānaratassa na upādānasammuditassa, upādānanirodhaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy grasping, and you truly see the cessation of grasping, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva, hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Ayampi kho, āvuso, pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: This too is a way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Siyā, āvuso.
segs.e: “There could, reverend.

segs.p: Taṇhārāmassa kho, āvuso, taṇhāratassa taṇhāsammuditassa, taṇhānirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you like, love, and enjoy craving, and don’t truly see the cessation of craving, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Na taṇhārāmassa kho, āvuso, na taṇhāratassa na taṇhāsammuditassa, taṇhānirodhaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti …pe…
segs.e: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy craving, and you truly see the cessation of craving, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti.
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

segs.p: Ayampi kho, āvuso, pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: This too is a way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Ettha dāni, āvuso sāriputta, ito uttari kiṁ icchasi?
segs.e: “Seriously, reverend, what more could you want?

segs.p: Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttassa, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhuno vaṭṭaṁ natthi paññāpanāyā”ti.
segs.e: For one who is freed due to the ending of craving, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.

segs.p: Moggallānasutta
segs.e: With Moggallāna

segs.p: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to Mahāmoggallāna:

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho moggallāna, sassato loko”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Moggallāna, is this right: ‘the cosmos is eternal’?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “Vaccha, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘sassato loko’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho moggallāna, asassato loko”ti?
segs.e: “Then is this right: ‘the cosmos is not eternal’ …

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
‘asassato loko’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, bho moggallāna, antavā loko”ti?
segs.e: ‘the cosmos is finite’ …

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
‘antavā loko’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho moggallāna, anantavā loko”ti?
segs.e: ‘the cosmos is infinite’ …

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
‘anantavā loko’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, bho moggallāna, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran”ti?
segs.e: ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’ …

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho moggallāna, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran”ti?
segs.e: ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’ …

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, bho moggallāna, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho moggallāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ …

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, bho moggallāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ …

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho moggallāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Ko nu kho, bho moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo, yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ puṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti—
segs.e: “What’s the cause, worthy Moggallāna, what’s the reason why, when the wanderers of other religions are asked these questions, they declare one of these to be true?

segs.p: sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti vā, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā?
Ko pana, bho moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo, yena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti—
segs.e: And what’s the reason why, when the ascetic Gotama is asked these questions, he does not declare one of these to be true?”

segs.p: sassato lokotipi, asassato lokotipi, antavā lokotipi, anantavā lokotipi, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīrantipi, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīrantipi, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇātipi, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇātipi, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇātipi, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇātipī”ti?
“Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā cakkhuṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti …pe…
segs.e: “Vaccha, the wanderers of other religions regard the eye like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’ They regard the ear … nose …

segs.p: jivhaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti …pe…
segs.e: tongue … body …

segs.p: manaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti.
segs.e: mind like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

segs.p: Tasmā aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ puṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti—
segs.e: That’s why, when asked, they declare one of those answers to be true.

segs.p: sassato lokoti vā …pe…
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā.

segs.p: ‘sassato loko’ti vā …pe…

Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yena bhoto gotamassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And what’s the reason why, when the worthy Gotama is asked these questions, he does not declare one of these to be true?”

segs.p: ‘sassato loko’tipi …pe…
‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipī”ti?
“Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā rūpaṁ attato samanupassanti, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: “Vaccha, the wanderers of other religions regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ attato samanupassanti …pe…
segs.e: They regard feeling …

segs.p: saññaṁ …pe…
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: saṅkhāre …pe…
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassanti, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Tasmā aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ puṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
segs.e: That’s why, when asked, they declare one of those answers to be true.

segs.p: ‘sassato loko’ti vā …pe…
‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā.

segs.e: The Realized One doesn’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: Na vedanaṁ attato samanupassati …pe…
segs.e: He doesn’t regard feeling …

segs.p: na saññaṁ …pe…

segs.e: choices …

segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Tasmā tathāgatassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
segs.e: That’s why, when asked, he does not declare one of those answers to be true.”

segs.e: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and went to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. He asked Mahāmoggallāna the same questions, and received the same answers.

‘sassato loko’tipi …pe…

segs.e: And he explained it to me with these words and phrases, just like the worthy Moggallāna.

segs.p: Acchariyaṁ, bho moggallāna, abbhutaṁ, bho moggallāna.

segs.p: Kutūhalasālāsutta
segs.e: The Debating Hall

segs.p: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Purimāni, bho gotama, divasāni purimatarāni sambahulānaṁ nānātitthiyānaṁ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ kutūhalasālāyaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, a few days ago several ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers who follow various other religions were sitting together in the debating hall, and this discussion came up among them:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho pūraṇo kassapo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa.
segs.e: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

segs.p: Sopi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
segs.e: When a disciple passes away, he declares that

segs.p: “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno”ti.
segs.e: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

segs.p: Yopissa sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tampi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
segs.e: And as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he also declares that

segs.p: “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno”ti.
segs.e: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

segs.p: Ayampi kho makkhali gosālo …pe…
segs.e: This bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla …

segs.p: ayampi kho nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto …pe…
segs.e: the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan …

segs.p: ayampi kho sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto …pe…
segs.e: Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta …

segs.p: ayampi kho pakudho kaccāno …pe…
segs.e: Pakudha Kaccāyana …

segs.p: ayampi kho ajito kesakambalo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa.
segs.e: Ajita of the hair blanket leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

segs.p: Sopi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
segs.e: When a disciple passes away, he declares that

segs.p: “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno”ti.
segs.e: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

segs.p: Yopissa sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tampi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
segs.e: And as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he also declares that

segs.p: “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno”ti.
segs.e: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

segs.p: Ayampi kho samaṇo gotamo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa.
segs.e: This ascetic Gotama leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

segs.p: Sopi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
segs.e: When a disciple passes away, he declares that

segs.p: “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno”ti.
segs.e: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

segs.p: Yopissa sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tañca sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu na byākaroti:
segs.e: But as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he doesn’t declare that

segs.p: “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno”ti.
segs.e: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

segs.p: Api ca kho naṁ evaṁ byākaroti:
segs.e: Rather, he declares that they have

segs.p: “acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā”’ti.
segs.e: cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit have made an end of suffering.’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bho gotama, ahu deva kaṅkhā, ahu vicikicchā:
segs.e: I had doubt and uncertainty about that:

segs.p: ‘kathaṁ nāma samaṇassa gotamassa dhammo abhiññeyyo’”ti?
segs.e: ‘How on earth can I understand the ascetic Gotama’s teaching?’”

segs.p: “Alañhi te, vaccha, kaṅkhituṁ, alaṁ vicikicchituṁ.
segs.e: “Vaccha, no wonder you’re doubting and uncertain.

segs.p: Kaṅkhanīye ca pana te ṭhāne vicikicchā uppannā.
segs.e: Doubt has come up in you about an uncertain matter.

segs.p: Saupādānassa khvāhaṁ, vaccha, upapattiṁ paññāpemi no anupādānassa.
segs.e: I describe rebirth for someone who grasps fuel, not for someone who does not.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, vaccha, aggi saupādāno jalati, no anupādāno;
segs.e: It’s like a fire which only burns with fuel, not without fuel.

segs.p: evameva khvāhaṁ, vaccha, saupādānassa upapattiṁ paññāpemi, no anupādānassā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way I describe rebirth for someone who grasps fuel, not for someone who doesn’t grasp fuel.”

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ, bho gotama, samaye acci vātena khittā dūrampi gacchati, imassa pana bhavaṁ gotamo kiṁ upādānasmiṁ paññāpetī”ti?
segs.e: “But when a flame is blown away by the wind, what does the worthy Gotama say is its fuel then?”

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ kho, vaccha, samaye acci vātena khittā dūrampi gacchati, tamahaṁ vātūpādānaṁ paññāpemi.
segs.e: “At such a time, I say that it’s fueled by the wind.

segs.p: Vāto hissa, vaccha, tasmiṁ samaye upādānaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: For the wind is its fuel then.”

segs.p: “Yasmiñca pana, bho gotama, samaye imañca kāyaṁ nikkhipati, satto ca aññataraṁ kāyaṁ anupapanno hoti, imassa pana bhavaṁ gotamo kiṁ upādānasmiṁ paññāpetī”ti?
segs.e: “But when someone who is attached has laid down this body and has not been reborn in one of the realms, what does the worthy Gotama say is their fuel then?”

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ kho, vaccha, samaye imañca kāyaṁ nikkhipati, satto ca aññataraṁ kāyaṁ anupapanno hoti, tamahaṁ taṇhūpādānaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: “When someone who is attached has laid down this body, Vaccha, and has not been reborn in one of the realms, I say they’re fueled by craving.

segs.p: Taṇhā hissa, vaccha, tasmiṁ samaye upādānaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: For craving is their fuel then.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.

segs.p: Ānandasutta
segs.e: With Ānanda

segs.p: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, atthattā”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, does the self survive?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: But when he said this, the Buddha kept silent.

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, natthattā”ti?
segs.e: “Then does the self not survive?”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: But for a second time the Buddha kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkante vacchagotte paribbājake bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then, not long after Vacchagotta had left, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, bhante, bhagavā vacchagottassa paribbājakassa pañhaṁ puṭṭho na byākāsī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, why didn’t you answer Vacchagotta’s question?”

segs.p: “Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘atthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘atthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, ye te, ānanda, samaṇabrāhmaṇā sassatavādā tesametaṁ saddhiṁ abhavissa.
segs.e: “Ānanda, when Vacchagotta asked me whether the self survives, if I had answered that ‘the self survives’ I would have been siding with the ascetics and brahmins who are eternalists.

segs.p: Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘natthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘natthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, ye te, ānanda, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ucchedavādā tesametaṁ saddhiṁ abhavissa.
segs.e: When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self does not survive, if I had answered that ‘the self does not survive’ I would have been siding with the ascetics and brahmins who are annihilationists.

segs.p: Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘atthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘atthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, api nu me taṁ, ānanda, anulomaṁ abhavissa ñāṇassa uppādāya:
segs.e: When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self survives, if I had answered that ‘the self survives’, would that have facilitated the arising of the knowledge that

segs.p: ‘sabbe dhammā anattā’”ti?
segs.e: all things are not-self?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘natthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘natthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, sammūḷhassa, ānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa bhiyyo sammohāya abhavissa:
segs.e: “When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self does not survive, if I had answered that ‘the self does not survive’, Vacchagotta—who is already confused—would have got even more confused, thinking:

segs.p: ‘ahuvā me nūna pubbe attā, so etarahi natthī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘It seems that the self that I once had no longer survives.’”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.

segs.p: Sabhiyakaccānasutta
segs.e: With Sabhiya Kaccāna

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā sabhiyo kaccāno ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

segs.p: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yenāyasmā sabhiyo kaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sabhiyena kaccānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to him, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako āyasmantaṁ sabhiyaṁ kaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to Sabhiya Kaccāna:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho bho, kaccāna, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Kaccāna, does a realized one still exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “Vaccha, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: “Worthy Kaccāna, when asked these questions, you say that this has not been declared by the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā—
hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā—
na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, vaccha, bhagavatā—
hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṁ bhagavatā—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
Ko nu kho, bho kaccāna, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ samaṇena gotamenā”ti?
segs.e: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Yo ca, vaccha, hetu, yo ca paccayo paññāpanāya rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā, so ca hetu, so ca paccayo sabbena sabbaṁ sabbathā sabbaṁ aparisesaṁ nirujjheyya.
segs.e: “In order to describe him as ‘formed’ or ‘formless’ or ‘percipient’ or ‘non-percipient’ or ‘neither percipient nor non-percipient’, there must be some cause or reason for doing so. But if that cause and reason were to totally and utterly cease without remainder,

segs.p: Kena naṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā”ti.
segs.e: how could you describe him in any such terms?”

segs.p: “Kīvaciraṁ pabbajitosi, bho kaccānā”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Kaccāna, how long has it been since you went forth?”

segs.p: “Naciraṁ, āvuso, tīṇi vassānī”ti.
segs.e: “Not long, reverend: three years.”

segs.p: “Yassapassa, āvuso, etamettakena ettakameva tampassa bahu, ko pana vādo evaṁ abhikkante”ti.
segs.e: “One who has learned this much in this time, reverend, has learned a lot, who can say what lies ahead!”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Abyākatavaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Khemātherī anurādho,
sāriputtoti koṭṭhiko;
Moggallāno ca vaccho ca,
kutūhalasālānando;
Sabhiyo ekādasamanti.
Abyākatasaṁyuttaṁ samattaṁ.
segs.e: The Linked Discourses on undeclared questions are complete.

segs.p: Tassuddānaṁ
Saḷāyatanavedanā,
mātugāmo jambukhādako;
Sāmaṇḍako moggallāno,
citto gāmaṇi saṅkhataṁ;
Abyākatanti dasadhāti.
Saḷāyatanavaggo catuttho.
Saḷāyatanavaggasaṁyuttapāḷi niṭṭhitā.
segs.e: The Book of the Six Sense Fields is finished.
